newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London off amid profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London off amid profit-taking.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London lost ground on Friday as some investors decided to take profits in blue chip stocks after a week of moderate gains, traders said.
"Most of the factors that have been supporting the market during the week have gone now," one trader said. "It will open lower in Tokyo on Monday."
The Nikkei 50 index was down 13.46 points, or one percent, at 1336.06 by 1534 GMT while Nikkei 225 futures fell 175 points to 17,560 in early trading in Chicago.

Traders said stocks came under selling pressure late in the session as investors decided to cash in on gains made by blue chip stocks earlier in the week. "People have had enough of this market," one trader said.
Worst hit were the banks as worries over the financial health of the sector persisted from the Tokyo close.
Tokai Bank was down 14 yen from its Tokyo close at 940 yen while Sanwa Bank was down 5 yen at 1385. The 225-share Nikkei average in Tokyo finished down 220.10 points, or 1.23 percent, at 17,689.36.
